1#א: ["Or of glass or vessels coated with lead, etc. Thus it should read, and that is earthenware vessels and similar coated with lead:"]
1#ב: ["Coated with lead. And Issur VeHeter wrote general rule 58 law 89: vessels coated with glass have the same law as coated with lead:"]
1#ג: ["Some say, etc. Thus it should read, and he argues with the first reason:"]
1#ד: ["He immerses without a blessing. Mordechai wrote in the name of Rama that even if coated only outside with lead, one immerses it without a blessing; Beit Yosef and Darkei Moshe bring it; and Bach wrote one should wonder at the world's custom who use pots coated with lead inside without any immersion at all:"]
1#ה: ["Without a blessing. And it appears one should immerse them with some other vessel with a blessing, as below seif 9; and so it is in Issur VeHeter general rule 58 — see there:"]
2#א: ["Loose in his hand, etc. Requires study, for Beit Yosef and the later authorities did not bring any dispute on this; and Rambam chapter 2 of Hilchot Mikvaot law 11 wrote: one who holds a person and vessels and immerses them — they remain in their impurity, and even if he loosened his hands it is a decree lest he not loosen — end of his words; and Rav Yerocham brings it in his conclusion; and likewise Rashba at the end of Terumat HaDeshen in the name of Rambam; and likewise Rosh in Bava Kama there; and Bach ruled below siman 198 seif 20 regarding immersion of a person that even if loose his tevilah did not take effect; and at the end of chapter 8 of Mikvaot we plainly teach a person and vessels together — see there; requires study:"]
2#ב: ["But not in detached water. See Lechem Chamudot end of Niddah daf 315a what he challenged on this; and one may say that here, if not for the water, it would be a chatzitzah; therefore the water comes to remove from the category of chatzitzah; therefore we require mikveh water — investigate:"]
3#_: He blesses on tevilat kelim. And some poskim bless on tevilah of metal vessels; and likewise Bach that this is essential and that he saw them act according to the elders; and likewise Issur VeHeter general rule 98 law 100:
4#_: But fidleash requires tevilah. Because they roast upon it the food itself — such is Semak's language, meaning what they call in foreign tongue "roist":
5#א: ["That it does not require tevilah. The reason is explained there: they are not eating vessels, for although the animal is fit for eating, for this reason it is not considered an eating vessel, for it still requires cooking or roasting — end of his words:"]
5#ב: ["The irons, etc. Question: in Issur VeHeter general rule 58 law 2 he compared the irons to a slaughter knife used for skinning that does not require tevilah, since the thing being fixed still requires another repair; if so, since the rabbi wrote regarding a slaughter knife one should immerse without a blessing, the same applies to the irons; and it appears the rabbi holds the irons are even more inferior, for it is impossible to use them for another food, unlike a slaughter knife that can be used for other food; and likewise in Issur VeHeter's gloss there, needles with which fowl are sewn are not judged like a slaughter knife, and a skinning knife since it cannot be used for other food — end; and accordingly what Bach wrote in seif 4 that vegetable scissors are food needs, as regarding injury it is called things with which one makes food for the soul in Choshen Mishpat siman 97 — end of his words — is not clear, for it cannot be used for other food; rather it appears as Perishah wrote that vegetable scissors do not require tevilah; and one may say regarding injury that there even things not food needs they return his plowing tools, adzes, and planes, and likewise slaughter knife — Tur wrote there in seif 8 it is food for the soul, and here he wrote no tevilah is required; accordingly all the more so the awl with which they pierce barrel hoops does not require tevilah, unlike Maharil at the end of Hilchot Tevilah who wrote they require tevilah — and so is the practice:"]
6#_: It does not require tevilah. Requires study, for Beit Yosef ruled the halachah that one should immerse it without a blessing, for we are uncertain whether we follow the one who stabilizes it or not; Darkei Moshe brings it in his conclusion; and likewise at the end of Maharil's laws of tevilah one immerses without a blessing; and likewise Issur VeHeter general rule 58 law 49 that one immerses them without a blessing or with other vessels:
7#א: ["Requires tevilah, etc. It implies a blessing is required; and even though Beit Yosef ruled regarding a silver cup whose stabilizer is wood that one immerses without a blessing, one may say that there, if not for the wood the cup would not be fit at all and the wood stabilizes it; but here the case is where the cup is fit as is and is only attached to a wooden vessel:"]
7#ב: ["Mill, etc. And Darkei Moshe wrote in the name of Hagahot Maimoniyot that the lower part receiving the spice does not require tevilah; and likewise Issur VeHeter there law 85 that the lower receiving the grindings does not require it, for it is all wood:"]
7#ג: ["And likewise iron funnels, etc. But a wooden funnel with an iron tube does not require tevilah even though one uses it via the iron, since it does not stabilize relative to the funnel; and likewise all similar cases — likewise Issur VeHeter there law 84:"]
8#א: ["Must immerse it. And Issur VeHeter there law 86 ruled tevilah is required; and it appears one should immerse without a blessing or immerse another vessel with it:"]
8#ב: ["Forbidden to use for meal needs. But for non-meal needs it is permitted to use even though he took it for a meal; when he changed his mind to cut cards with it, it does not require tevilah — so Issur VeHeter wrote there law 80:"]
8#ג: ["The second too requires tevilah. Even though the first took it to cut cards and the like:"]
9#א: ["And if not, etc. Meaning he does not know whether the non-Jew intends to sink it in his possession or not; but if he knows clearly the non-Jew does not intend to sink it, it is obvious no tevilah is required — all this I proved in my book from Tosafot and Tur and Maharil's laws of Pesach, who wrote a pledge requires tevilah only when decided in Jewish hands; and in responsum siman 60 he wrote we are in doubt in the Gemara and uncertain, and tevilah is required out of doubt — unlike Bach — see there; however in any case where the non-Jew does not intend to sink it, Maharil wrote one may not use it without the non-Jew's permission because of deceit, forbidden even regarding a non-Jew's property; we do not practice thus, etc.; and it appears he holds there is no deceit of the non-Jew in using it:"]
9#ב: ["And if in the end it sank, etc. Thus it should read. And Issur VeHeter wrote there law 88; nevertheless, if he added money to the non-Jew and bought the pledge from him after they immersed it out of doubt, he requires tevilah again with a blessing, for they did not immerse initially with this intent — end of his words:"]
10#א: ["And some disagree, etc. Bach challenged the rabbi on this and his words are not plausible, as I wrote in my book; the essential law is as Beit Yosef and the rabbi wrote — Tur's view in the name of Ritzba: even with Jewish silver, since the non-Jew makes the main vessel, tevilah is required, whether the non-Jew makes an entirely new vessel or it was pierced and did not hold a revi'it, since the non-Jew stabilizes it — according to Ritzba even Jewish silver; and Maharshal concludes in chapter HaGozel Eitzim siman 22; and we do not explain Ritzba's words only with non-Jew's silver — rather Ritzba disagrees and always holds tevilah is required, for a craftsman acquires through enhancement of the vessel, etc.; and although for halachah Maharshal concludes there no tevilah is required, nevertheless one should certainly be stringent regarding a d'oraisa prohibition; and perhaps even Maharshal only means no tevilah is required by law, therefore one should not bless on it; and so it appears from his language that he wrote therefore, etc., no tevilah is required, and one who immerses with a blessing — the court would rule on him because of a blessing in vain — end of his words:"]
10#ג: ["He immerses it too without a blessing. Because we are uncertain whether we follow the craftsman — and here tevilah is not required — or we follow the one whose silver it is:"]
10#ד: ["Or he gave, etc. Meaning the non-Jew gave the Jew part of the metals from his own and the Jew made it for himself — no tevilah; and it deals where part of the vessel is still the non-Jew's because of his metals; if so it resembles a Jew and non-Jew who received a vessel in partnership — tevilah is required for the reason Issur VeHeter wrote at the end of law 88: for he certainly does not emerge from the name of impurity through this tevilah, for partnership of the non-Jew is still upon it — end; and likewise Taz; and if so the same here; or it appears this is what the rabbi meant: and likewise a Jewish craftsman who made a vessel for a non-Jew, etc., if the non-Jew gave all the metals and he bought it from him — tevilah without blessing; but if he made it for himself only buying metals from the non-Jew, or even made it for the non-Jew and the non-Jew did not give all metals but gave part from his own and afterward bought it — no tevilah; and it appears to the rabbi that Mordechai certainly did not mean where there is part non-Jewish silver tevilah is required only because the non-Jew made it, but when the Jew made it — even according to those who follow whose silver it is, it is possible where part of the silver is the Jew's that he agrees no tevilah is required; and this is the main explanation:"]
11#א: ["But if he pledged it, etc. Even if he intended to sink it in the non-Jew's possession — no tevilah — likewise Issur VeHeter there law 88; and likewise Bach and Perishah in the name of Maharshal, who wrote in his name: if initially he pledged with intent not to redeem and changed his mind and redeemed — tevilah is required:"]
11#ב: ["In partnership — no tevilah. I already wrote the reason in s.k. 22; and from that reason it implies while part of the vessel is still the non-Jew's; but if the Jew returned and bought the non-Jew's share — tevilah is required:"]
11#ג: ["A Jew whom they stole, etc.; but a minister, etc. Taz wrote the reason: a minister or governor who certainly despaired of them — it is as if they sank in non-Jewish hands, etc.; therefore if theft and robbery are in a matter we heard he despaired of them, tevilah is required; and it is not clear, for in Issur VeHeter from which the rabbi brought this law (general rule 58 law 89 on the gloss) he wrote the reason: for a thief and robber, even though they despaired completely, since they are not permitted to hold it publicly, the non-Jew's name is not called upon it and no tevilah is required; Darkei Moshe brings it; and perhaps Taz also agrees to this, only he comes to say that even a minister or governor does not require tevilah except because presumably he despaired and it is as if sunk in non-Jewish hands; but if he did not despair — tevilah is required:"]
15#_: Their tevilah was valid. Bach wrote the main reason of Rashba is because he ruled like Rav in chapter 2 of Chullin (daf 31) that a niddah who immersed without intent — her tevilah was valid; but for us who rule below end of siman 198 like R. Yochanan that a niddah requires intent — likewise here their tevilah was not valid — end of his words; and it is difficult, for Rashba ruled like R. Yochanan regarding niddah and Beit Yosef brings it end of siman 198; rather Rashba's main reason is that tevilah here is different, as he brought in this siman his words that he distinguishes; and likewise Terumat HaDeshen siman 257: even those who require intent for niddah — who says this tevilah of vessels, which is not impurity to purity and does not forbid what entered before tevilah and is only a decree of Scripture — requires intent? — end; and so the rabbi's view appears, who ruled plainly here like the Mechaber (and below end of siman 198 regarding niddah he ruled another tevilah is required); and Darkei Moshe ruled plainly like the Mechaber; and further, since he did not write in seif 14 regarding a minor that the adult must teach him to intend to purify, as Darkei Moshe brought in the name of Terumat HaDeshen — evidently he holds like Terumat HaDeshen's conclusion there that for tevilah here intent is not required; and wherever intent is not required, one need not teach him at all, as proven in Tosafot chapter 1 of Chullin daf 12 beginning; and Taz also distinguishes between niddah tevilah and tevilah here — see there; and therefore if vessels fell into water before tevilah, no tevilah is required, as Maharam's responsum — unlike Bach who rejected his words from what he holds intent is required, for this was already explained to be incorrect:
16#_: He gives it to a non-Jew, etc. See Orach Chaim siman 323 seif 7 — the rabbi wrote another remedy; and see responsum Maharal ibn Chaviv siman 16. Supplement to the laws of tevilat kelim — see below simanim 201 and 202:
